newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary plans 4000mW new electric capacity by 2010.
newsitem.headline: Hungary plans 4000mW new electric capacity by 2010.

text.p: Hungary plans to invite investors to build power station capacity of almost 4,000 megawatts by 2010, government spokesman Elemer Kiss told a news conference following a cabinet meeting on Thursday.
Kiss said the government had decided that 900-1000 megawatts of capacity should be built by 2000, a further 2200 megawatts between 2001 and 2005, and 780 megawatts between 2006 and 2010.

The figures include obsolete capacity which must be modernised by 2010, with 300 to 500 Megawatts to be taken out of service by 2000, 1500 to 1600 megawatts between 2001 and 2005 and 300 to 350 mW between 2006 and 2010, Kiss said.
The government decision must be approved by the parliament.
Kiss said that investors which had acquired stakes in Hungarian energy companies had undertaken substantial developments.
A government statement said that developments will be necessary as Hungary's environmental protection regulations are likely to become substantially stricter in 1996.
Hungary has sold three of the seven power stations which it planned to privatise to foreign investors.
